data.narrative:
Impossible Metals is a seed-stage company in Climate & Energy focused on subsea robotics for deep-sea mineral extraction. The target has raised $15M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lilium, LNZA), though peer-set constraints limit traditional multiples-based approaches.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the sector. Using total capital raised ($15M) as a proxy for seed-stage enterprise value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding round yields a median valuation of $38M. A ±15% sensitivity range around this midpoint produces a low of $32M and a high of $43M, reflecting estimation uncertainty inherent to single-method derivation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M–$43M, with $38M as the point estimate. Key uncertainties include absence of narrow-stage peer data (no seed or series-A comparables in the immediate sector) and reliance on a single capital-raised proxy rather than revenue or unit economics multiples. The founder team's subsea-robotics expertise (Gillham's 18-year track record and prior exit via Voyis acquisition) and sustainability focus represent differentiation factors not captured in this quantitative range.
